summary: A conditional grant of rights to specific Hewlett-Packard patents for use in IETF standards-track network management MIB modules. It is a legal statement, not a technical specification.

eli5.summary: A company said it would let others use its patented idea in certain network management standards under certain conditions.

patent rights in ietf mib modules
subtitle: Hewlett-Packard promises not to sue over two patents when used in IETF standards-track MIB modules.

tldr.problem: HP held patents covering a network device mapping technique called search address, and the IETF wanted to use it in standards-track network management MIB modules.
tldr.mechanism: HP announced a covenant not to assert claims under US Patents 5,293,635 and 5,421,024 against anyone implementing such a MIB module for the Internet-standard network management framework.
tldr.outcome: The grant is conditional: it does not cover proprietary MIB modules and ends for any party that asserts its own patent against HP over search address technology.

today: RFC 1988 is an Informational memo, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The text does not say what has happened to the grant since August 1996.

sections.title: What This Document Is
sections.content: This memo is explicitly not a standard. It is an announcement to interested parties of a conditional grant by the Hewlett-Packard Company (HP) of certain rights to use autotopology network management technology covered by specific HP patents, together with the IETF's Internet-standard network management framework.
sections.eli5: This is not a rule about how networks work. It is a public note from a company about what it will let other people do with its invention.

sections.title: Purpose and Grant
sections.content:
The purpose is to help bring HP's patented search address technology, which covers network device mapping, into IETF standards-track Management Information Base (MIB) modules. HP offers it to the IETF as a technique for mapping network devices. The memo notes that the confirmatory license it mentions is optional, since the grant of rights is automatic.

HP covenants that it will not assert claims in US Patents 5,293,635 and 5,421,024, their continuations, divisions or continuations-in-part, or any non-US counterparts, against any party that makes, uses, sells, imports or offers for sale an implementation of an IETF standards-track MIB module that includes HP's contributed search address technology or a derivative of it. The MIB module must be used to implement the Internet-standard network management framework.
sections.eli5: The company promises not to take anyone to court for using its idea inside official network-management standards.

sections.title: Limits and Termination
sections.content:
The grant has two limits. It does not include a right to incorporate HP's search address technology into proprietary MIB modules. And it permanently terminates for any party, and any subsidiary of that party, that asserts a patent it owns or controls against HP or its subsidiaries over implementing or operating a system using search address technology. Termination takes effect on the date the patent is asserted against HP.

Anyone who wants written confirmation, or a license under any other HP patent at HP's then-current terms, conditions and royalty rates, can write to HP's Patent Counsel in Palo Alto, California.
sections.eli5: The promise only covers official standards, not private versions. And if you sue the company over this idea, the promise to you ends.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The memo says only that security issues are not discussed. It is a legal statement about patent rights and defines no protocol behavior, so there is nothing technical to secure.
sections.eli5: The note does not talk about safety, because it is about permission, not about how anything works.
